name: Growth Hormone Insensitivity Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and biochemical criteria for Growth Hormone Insensitivity

criteria.description: Severe postnatal growth failure with short stature
Low serum insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) despite normal or elevated growth hormone levels
Lack of IGF-1 increase after exogenous growth hormone stimulation test
Identification of pathogenic variants in the growth hormone receptor (GHR) gene
Characteristic facial features including prominent forehead, depressed nasal bridge, and small chin

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of severe postnatal growth failure with low serum IGF-1 despite normal or elevated GH levels, plus lack of IGF-1 response to GH stimulation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical and biochemical criteria are met.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe postnatal growth failure with short stature

pathognomonic.symptomName: Characteristic facial dysmorphism including prominent forehead and depressed nasal bridge
searchTerms: distinct facial features with large forehead and flat nose bridge

laboratory: Low serum IGF-1 levels despite normal or elevated GH

genetic: Pathogenic variants in the GHR gene

distinguishingFeatures: Low GH levels in growth hormone deficiency versus normal/elevated GH in insensitivity
Positive IGF-1 response to GH stimulation in deficiency
Isolated low IGF-1 due to binding protein deficiency
Low IGF-1 with normal GH receptor function

redFlags: Severe growth failure despite normal or elevated GH levels
Low serum IGF-1 unresponsive to GH stimulation
Characteristic facial dysmorphism with growth failure
